statement: Retain all documentation of corrective actions taken as a result of an internal audit.

statement: When an internal audit finding leads to a process change, update all affected procedures, including the master production record, to reflect the change, and keep these records available for FDA inspection.
quote: For example, if a routine internal audit finds a problem with a mixing step and the outcome is a change in mixing time, all affected procedures, including the master production record, are to reflect the necessary changes, and such records are subject to FDA inspection as usual.

statement: Retain any investigation into the impact of an audit-identified problem on related batches and make it available for FDA inspection.
quote: Any investigation into the impact this problem had on related batches is to be retained and also made available for inspection by FDA (see § 211.192).

statement: Treat reports of investigations or evaluations prepared for matters such as product complaints, vendor qualification, periodic review of records and data, and failure investigations as records open to FDA inspection (not as internal audits), and retain them for at least the retention period set by the CGMP regulations.
quote: any reports of investigations or evaluations prepared in response to, for example, a product complaint (§ 211.198), vendor qualification (§ 211.84), periodic review of records and data (§ 211.180(e)), and a failure investigation (§ 211.192) are not internal audits as discussed above. Such records are subject to FDA inspection and must be retained for at least the time specified in the CGMP regulations (see § 211.180).

statement: Containers, closures and packaging materials may be sampled for receipt examination in the warehouse, provided the warehouse environment is suitable for the purported quality characteristics of the material sampled, so that sampling does not contaminate the contents.
quote: Yes. Generally, we believe that sampling in a typical drug manufacturing facility warehouse would not represent a risk to the container or closure or affect the integrity of the sample results. But whether the act of collecting a sample in the warehouse violates the CGMP requirement that containers "be opened, sampled, and sealed in a manner designed to prevent contamination of their contents..." will depend on the purported quality characteristics of the material under sample and the warehouse environment.
condition: warehouse environment suits the material's purported quality

statement: Sample containers or closures that are claimed to be sterile or depyrogenated under conditions equivalent to their claimed quality; a warehouse environment is not sufficient for this.
quote: For containers or closures purporting to be sterile or depyrogenated, sampling should be under conditions equivalent to the purported quality of the material: a warehouse environment would not suffice (see 21 CFR 211.94 and 211.113(b)).
condition: containers or closures purporting to be sterile or depyrogenated

statement: Perform all sampling of containers, closures and packaging materials so as to limit exposure to the environment during and after sample removal, e.g. by wiping outside surfaces, limiting the time the original package is open, and properly resealing it.
quote: At a minimum, any sampling should be performed in a manner to limit exposure to the environment during and after the time samples are removed (i.e., wiping outside surfaces, limiting time that the original package is open, and properly resealing the original package).

statement: Once the supplier's reliability has been established by validating its test results, the visual examination of containers or closures may be performed entirely in the warehouse.

statement: Where environmental monitoring for Mycoplasma is performed, use selective media (PPLO broth or agar).

quote: These regulations require representative samples of each shipment of each lot of active and inactive component (or raw materials) to be tested to confirm the identity of the component as labeled prior to release for use in drug product manufacturing. The regulations acknowledge that more than one test may be needed to ascertain a component’s identity.
condition: before release for use

statement: In the sampling program for components, take samples that are representative of the shipment received.

statement: In the sampling program for components, base the number of containers sampled and the amount sampled from each container on statistical criteria for component variability, confidence levels and the degree of precision required.

statement: In the sampling program for components, take into account the supplier's past quality history.

statement: Use an identity-testing approach for components that gives a high degree of confidence that each container in each shipment contains the material stated on its label.
quote: For these reasons, manufacturers need to develop an approach that provides a high degree of confidence that each container in each shipment contains the material purported by the label.

statement: Make all sampling representative and scientifically sound.
quote: (See also 21 CFR 211.160(b), which requires all sampling to be representative and scientifically sound.)

statement: Design the identity-testing approach to account for the fact that a material's identity must not vary from what is specified.
quote: The approach must account for the fact that the material’s identity must not vary from what is specified.

statement: Collect representative samples of each shipment of each lot of components for testing.
quote: The regulation at § 211.84 requires that representative samples of each shipment of each lot shall be collected for testing.

statement: Sampling and testing every container of a component for identity may be done, and may be particularly valuable for components bought from distributors.
quote: Testing samples from every container to determine identity may be valuable particularly for components purchased from distributors.

statement: The manufacturer may decide how many containers of a component to sample, as long as the sampling plan is scientifically sound, gives representative samples and follows the established principles for component sampling programs.
quote: The CGMP regulations permit each drug product manufacturer to make its own decision as to the number of containers to sample, as long as the sampling plan is scientifically sound, leads to representative samples, and complies with the principles established at § 211.84(b).
condition: plan scientifically sound, representative and in line with sampling principles

statement: Have the drug product manufacturer take component samples from the containers after receipt; pre-shipment or so-called piggyback samples are generally not acceptable.
quote: samples are to be taken by the drug product manufacturer from containers after receipt (i.e., pre-shipment samples or so-called piggyback samples are generally not acceptable)

statement: Do not composite samples taken from the top, middle and bottom of a single container when such stratified sampling is considered necessary (for example where moisture content needs to be controlled, especially when only part of a container may be used in a batch).
quote: Section 211.84(c)(4) explicitly prohibits compositing samples taken from the top, middle, and bottom of a single container when such stratified sampling is considered necessary (as might be the case when moisture content needs to be controlled, particularly when only a portion of a container may be used in a drug product batch).
condition: when stratified sampling is considered necessary

statement: Samples from a single container may be composited where compositing would not mask subdivisions of the sample that fail specifications.
quote: there "is no general prohibition... on compositing samples [from single containers] where such compositing would not mask subdivisions of the sample that do not meet specifications"
condition: where compositing would not mask failing subdivisions

statement: Testing individual samples from multiple containers is an acceptable approach that gives a high level of assurance.
quote: Testing individual samples from multiple containers provides a high level of assurance and is consistent with CGMP.

statement: A composite sample from multiple containers may be tested for identity only if the manufacturer demonstrates either that compositing does not mask detection of a single nonconforming container, or that additional test(s) routinely performed on the composite ensure that all sampled containers contain the same material.
quote: Testing a composite sample for identity could satisfy the CGMP regulations (§§ 211.84 and 211.160) but only if a manufacturer demonstrates either that the detection of a single nonconforming container is not masked by compositing or that an additional test(s) routinely performed on the composite sample ensures that all containers sampled contain the same material.
condition: only if masking is excluded or additional tests confirm sameness

statement: A purity assay on a composite sample made by mixing equal aliquots from each container may be acceptable, provided the test is sensitive enough to reveal a single nonconforming container.
quote: Thus, a purity assay on a composite sample prepared by mixing equal aliquots from each container may be acceptable provided such a test is sufficiently sensitive to reveal the presence of a single nonconforming container.
condition: provided the test detects a single nonconforming container

statement: Test at-risk components for melamine using a method shown to be suitable for detecting melamine adulteration, chosen on the basis of the manufacturer's risk assessment and prevention strategy.
quote: FDA recommends using a method demonstrated to be suitable for detecting melamine adulteration based on the manufacturer’s risk assessment and prevention strategy.

statement: When selecting the sampling approach and test method sensitivity for melamine, address the possibility that melamine is not uniformly distributed in an at-risk component, and that intentional contamination may originate in the starting material used to make that component.
quote: The manufacturer’s selection of a sampling approach and test method sensitivity should address the possibility that (1) melamine might not be uniformly distributed in an at-risk component, or (2) that the source of intentional melamine contamination might be the starting material used to produce the at-risk component.

statement: A less sensitive melamine method may be used for screening in certain cases.
quote: FDA also recognizes that a less sensitive method might also be appropriate for screening in certain cases.
condition: in certain cases

statement: Control animal-derived ingredients so that contamination does not occur, from the initial collection and handling of the animal material through its processing and later use in the finished product.
quote: Yes, FDA requires that animal-derived ingredients be controlled in a manner to ensure that contamination does not occur, beginning with initial collection and handling of the animal-derived material through its processing and subsequent use in a finished pharmaceutical.

statement: As an ingredient manufacturer, take responsibility for the quality and safety of ingredients made for use in finished drugs, and manufacture them in conformance with current good manufacturing practice.
quote: Ingredient manufacturers are responsible for the quality and safety of the material they produce for use in finished pharmaceuticals. Ingredients are drugs and drugs are required to conform with current good manufacturing practice (FD&C Act, section 501(a)(2)(B)).

statement: As a finished drug manufacturer, take responsibility for the selection, qualification and use of ingredients in finished products.
quote: Finished pharmaceutical manufacturers are also responsible for their selection, qualification, and use of ingredients in finished pharmaceuticals (e.g., the CGMP regulations at 21 CFR part 211, subpart E).

statement: Fully understand the potential for pathogenic agent contamination of animal-derived ingredients, starting at the livestock processing establishment and continuing through later handling and processing, and establish stringent controls to prevent it.
quote: Ingredient and finished pharmaceutical manufacturers should fully understand the potential for pathogenic agent contamination beginning with the livestock processing establishment (LPE) and continuing through subsequent handling and processing, and establish stringent controls to prevent contamination.

statement: As part of the contamination control program for animal-derived ingredients, develop and apply appropriate tests or examinations to detect contamination.
quote: It is also essential that appropriate tests or examinations are developed and applied to detect contamination as part of any meaningful control program.

statement: Assume that animal-derived materials will harbor and often support the growth of pathogens, and ensure appropriate control over their handling and processing.
quote: One should assume that animal-derived materials will not only harbor but will often support growth of pathogens and accordingly should ensure appropriate control over the handling and processing of these materials.

statement: Follow CGMP when handling animal-derived material so that no contamination occurs that would affect its quality and purity or harm patients receiving the product.
quote: Current good manufacturing practice is to be followed in handling such material to ensure that contamination does not occur that would affect the material’s quality and purity, or that would be harmful when the product is administered to patients.

statement: Prevent molds from growing in drug ingredients and, when feasible and valuable, remove all molds that may contaminate them.
quote: It is important to prevent molds from growing in drug ingredients and when feasible and valuable remove all molds that may contaminate such ingredients.
condition: removal when feasible and valuable

statement: When assessing the risk of viral contamination of an animal-derived ingredient, consider both the viral load of the raw material (e.g. tissue, glands, blood) and the viral clearance capability of the ingredient manufacturing process.
quote: The probability of an animal virus contaminating an animal-derived ingredient will depend on the viral load of the raw material (e.g., tissue, glands, blood) and the viral clearance capability of the drug ingredient manufacturing process. Both of these factors should be considered when assessing the risk of viral contamination of the ingredient.
condition: when assessing viral contamination risk

statement: Protect against prion contamination by obtaining bovine meat and meat byproducts from animals not infected with bovine spongiform encephalopathy, and by protecting product against contamination with high-risk tissues, especially brain and spinal cord.
quote: Protection from prion contamination includes obtaining bovine meat and meat byproducts from animals not infected with bovine spongiform encephalopathy and protecting against contamination of product with high-risk tissues, especially brain and spinal cord tissue.

statement: When importing bovine material into the United States, be familiar with and comply with all import eligibility requirements and government regulations on food and drugs.
quote: Drug manufacturers importing bovine material into the United States should be familiar with and adhere to all import eligibility requirements and government regulations pertaining to food and drugs.
condition: when importing bovine material into the United States

statement: Base contamination control on strategies that prevent contamination, not on final testing or examination alone; a control strategy relying on testing alone is not compliant.
quote: The drug component and finished product CGMP guidances and regulations emphasize prevention of problems and avoidance of contamination rather than final testing or examination alone. In other words, control strategies that prevent contamination are central to CGMP, while control strategies based on testing alone do not comply with CGMP regulations.

statement: When animal-derived material is used, obtain it from healthy, disease-free animals.
quote: When animal-derived material is used, it is important that it be derived from healthy, disease-free animals.
condition: when animal-derived material is used

statement: Understand the pathogenic risks associated with different animal species and with different organs, glands or tissues within a species.
quote: Ingredient manufacturers should understand the pathogenic risks associated with different animal species and with different organs, glands, or tissues within species.

statement: Recognise that even healthy source animals can be reservoirs of pathogenic agents and that improper handling can spread contamination.
quote: Drug ingredient manufacturers should be aware that even healthy animals can be reservoirs for pathogenic agents and improper handling can spread contamination.

statement: Consider auditing the livestock processing establishments that supply raw materials, and ensure they comply with all Federal and State government regulations.
quote: Ingredient manufacturers should consider auditing the LPEs supplying raw materials to them and ensure their compliance with all Federal and State government regulations.

statement: For products at risk of glass delamination, vial surface alkalinity may be minimised by proper selection of glass composition (e.g. highly resistant, non-alkaline-earth borosilicate glass), appropriate selection and qualification of vial vendors, and proper quality control of incoming vials.

statement: Manufacture all APIs in compliance with CGMP.

statement: Manufacture all drugs, including APIs, in compliance with CGMP.

statement: Test each component for conformity with all appropriate written specifications for purity, strength and quality.

statement: Instead of full testing, a supplier's report of analysis for a component may be accepted, provided the manufacturer conducts at least one specific identity test on the component and establishes the reliability of the supplier's analyses by appropriate validation of the supplier's test results at appropriate intervals.

statement: Ensure that compendial-grade APIs comply with compendial specifications, either by testing them or by validating the API supplier's reliability.
